utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you mean even if Mr. Ecim had been involved in inappropriate conduct, or even criminal conduct, it wouldn't matter to Mr. Zupljanin, in terms of appointing him to a position as the commander of the police brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, you know, it's not for me to decide about the acts of certain people, whether they were police officers, military people, specials, whatever, any acts of theirs that are not in keeping with the laws and regulations. So I don't want to speculate whether anybody was promoted due to any feats of theirs, whatever they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Related to that, we looked at the early April events in Banja Luka where the SOS had set up barricades around town. Isn't that unlawful or illegal, in violation of some criminal law or traffic and safety law or municipal ordinance, to block the roads?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. But --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, that's okay. I just needed the yes. Let me ask you a follow-up question. So why didn't the police arrest those people who set up the barricades and take the barricades down, instead of letting them negotiate with the mayor and the politicians about whatever demands they had about the army and the police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, you see, Mr. Prosecutor, yesterday and the day before, and today too, I said during my testimony that the security situation in the city of Banja Luka was very complex. To avoid repeating myself, this was about large numbers of people in uniform, wearing various insignia, with long-barrelled weapons, driving stolen vehicles, vehicles that were painted over, and so on. The police were not trained for countering individuals or organised groups with weapons, whether they were armed groups of the Territorial Defence or reserve forces or any other units. The police could not act, because they were facing warriors, if I may call them that. And when I say "warriors," I mean people who were trained to use weapons or had already seen combat. Especially when, after a day or two, I don't know, or maybe a couple of hours later, it was said that political agreements had been reached with, if I remember correctly, the representatives of the SOS and the politicians and the military in town hall. And for removing them, in my opinion, since we're talking about armed individuals and groups, it's the military police who had to do it, because they were military conscripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So did the civilian police in Banja Luka contact the JNA and/or the TO military police to inform them about their members who were acting in concert with these SOS, Serbian Defence Forces, in erecting and maintaining these barricades? Did you try to get the army to do something about these people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know, believe me. Maybe ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: ... the military police should have acted upon a report received from a citizen or an institution, et cetera. That's for sure, but I don't know if they did. And I don't know if -- because I remember the event. Because I think I was at work on that day and on the day after the event. There was a report which didn't originate from us. I think it went from the centre chief to the services in charge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. I next, now, want to move to some communications documents. If we could look at -- and I guess I should go into private session, Your Honour, for this next series of questions. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So we adjourn, to resume tomorrow morning at 9.00. And the blinds would be lowered to escort the witness out after we would have left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 22nd day of September, 2011, at 9.00 a.m. 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.45 p.m.,
